meta.audience: The church at Zarahemla, and those outside it

world_behind.title: This is what the resignation was for
world_behind.text: The previous chapter ends with Alma handing the judgment-seat to Nephihah and confining himself to the priesthood and the testimony of the word. Verse 1 is the next sentence in the story, and the sixty verses after it are the first thing he does with the freed hands.

world_behind.title: The record changes hands mid-page
world_behind.text: Verse 2 says these are the words he spoke "according to his own record." From that point the text is a first-person document quoted whole. The chapter is a primary source dropped into the middle of a summary.

world_behind.title: It opens with a history lesson
world_behind.text: Verses 3 to 5 walk the congregation back through the waters of Mormon, the escape from Noah's people, the Lamanite bondage, and the arrival in this land. Whatever else Alma is about to ask, he starts by establishing what these people already owe.

world_behind.title: The argument is made almost entirely in questions
world_behind.text: Roughly forty of the sixty-two verses are interrogative. He does not tell the congregation what it is; he asks, and the questions are built so that the answers can only be supplied privately.

world_behind.title: Nobody in the room heard Abinadi
world_behind.text: The events Alma builds on (the preaching at Noah's court, the waters of Mormon, the flight, the bondage) happened to the parents of this congregation. Verse 6 asks three times whether they have "sufficiently retained in remembrance," which is the question you ask a second generation.

world_behind.title: Two categories, and everyone is in one of them
world_behind.text: Verses 38 to 41 set up a good shepherd and a fold, and then a second shepherd and a second fold. There is no third option offered anywhere in the sermon, and verse 39 says so directly.

world_behind.title: It ends by addressing people who are not members
world_behind.text: Verse 62 splits the audience in two and hands each half a different kind of speech: one binding, one open. A sermon delivered inside a congregation turns outward in its last sentence, and the turn is made explicitly.

words.text: Lit up from outside. The fathers were in the midst of darkness and their souls were illuminated by the light of the everlasting word. The word appears once in this record and once in the New Testament, where Paul uses it of converts who afterward endured a great fight of afflictions (Heb. 10:32). Both times it names a past event with consequences still running.

The state of not decaying. Treated at Mosiah 16:10. Alma asks whether they look forward with an eye of faith and see this corruption raised in incorruption. The pairing is Paul's, from the resurrection chapter, and the record uses the noun six times. Here it is put as a question about eyesight rather than as a proposition about bodies.

A judgment bench, a court with the furniture implied. The word is unique in scripture. Six verses earlier the chapter has been talking about hearts; here it produces a room, a bar, and a docket, and the defendant arrives already carrying a perfect remembrance of his own record.

Stripped bare, with nothing left on. Alma uses it twice in two verses, of pride and then of envy, and the record uses it once more, of a debtor who could not pay. The image is not of pride being reduced but of its being taken off entirely, the way clothing comes off.

An enclosure for sheep, and by extension the flock inside it. "Of what fold are ye" is the question the whole middle of the sermon has been building toward. Alma's own congregation had entered the fold of God at the waters of Mormon; the word calls that covenant back without naming it.

Certainty, sure knowledge. Treated at Mosiah 5:2. It is the noun the record reaches for when somebody is asked how they know. Alma asks the congregation how they suppose he knows of the surety of these things, and then spends three verses answering his own question. The people at Benjamin's tower used the same word of themselves.

Not able to be put out. Treated at Jacob 6:10. The fire in the parable is described twice over. It cannot be consumed, and it cannot be quenched, which makes it permanent from two directions at once. The adjective appears five times in this record and twice in the Gospels, always attached to the same image of the tree and the ax.

phrases.term: He awakened them out of a deep sleep, and they awoke unto God
phrases.text: Conversion described as waking rather than as deciding. The verb is done to them in the first clause and by them in the second, and the sentence holds both without choosing. The next clause puts them in the midst of darkness, where sleepers usually are.

Two consequences of being loosed, and neither is a doctrine. One is a change of size and the other is a noise. The record uses "sing redeeming love" three times, and Alma will ask the congregation in verse 26 whether they can still do it.

phrases.term: Have ye received his image in your countenances
phrases.text: The question the sermon is most often remembered for, and it is asked about faces. Not conduct, not belief, but appearance, and specifically what shows on the front of a head. The phrase occurs once in scripture and its partner in verse 19 puts the image as engraven, something cut in.

phrases.term: With a pure heart and clean hands
phrases.text: The two halves of the old temple question about who shall ascend into the hill of the Lord, reversed in order and asked of a congregation. David's psalm names them as the entry requirement. Alma repeats the question twice in the same verse and attaches it to the ability to look up.

Four words, and the whole chapter turns on them. He grants the past tense entirely. You did experience a change of heart, you did sing. Then he asks about the present. It is the only question in the sermon that cannot be answered by remembering something.

phrases.term: I speak in the energy of my soul
phrases.text: An account of how hard he is working, offered as a reason to listen. The phrase appears twice in scripture and Nephi used the other one, also of speaking to people who had stopped hearing him. Alma places it at the exact point where the sermon stops asking questions and starts testifying.

phrases.term: The aged, and also the middle aged, and the rising generation
phrases.text: A congregation sorted by age, and the middle term is unique in scripture. He has already said old and young, bond and free; this clause goes back and inserts the people who would otherwise fall between the two. Nobody is being allowed to hear this as addressed to somebody else.

The last four words that matter in the sermon, and they are a change of mode. To the church he speaks by way of command; to everyone else, by way of invitation. The same content arrives as an obligation or as an offer depending entirely on what the hearer has already promised.

verses.label: v. 2
verses.title: The abridger names the document he is copying from
verses.text: Before the sermon begins the record identifies its source: "these are the words which he spake to the people in the church which was established in the city of Zarahemla, according to his own record." The last four words matter. What follows is not reconstructed from memory or tradition but taken from a text the speaker wrote himself, and the abridger says so in the sentence that introduces it.

verses.label: v. 6–30
verses.title: A sermon made of questions, and the count is not close
verses.text: The record carries forty-two question marks in this chapter, spread across twenty-six of its sixty-two verses. No other chapter in the book of Alma comes near it; Alma 30, a formal disputation with a named opponent, has twenty-two. The heaviest stretch runs from verse 14 to verse 30, where question follows question with only the answer formula between them. A chapter with nobody to answer back asks more questions than the one where somebody does.

verses.label: v. 14–15
verses.title: Three questions in a single verse, then five more
verses.text: The record sets the examination out as a rapid series: "have ye spiritually been born of God? Have ye received his image in your countenances? Have ye experienced this mighty change in your hearts?" Verse 15 continues without pause, "Do ye exercise faith in the redemption of him who created you? Do you look forward with an eye of faith, and view this mortal body raised in immortality?" None is answered. The form requires each hearer to supply an answer that the record never records.

verses.label: v. 27–30
verses.title: Each question comes with its verdict attached
verses.text: Unlike the earlier run, these questions are followed immediately by the consequence of a wrong answer. "Are ye stripped of pride? I say unto you, if ye are not ye are not prepared to meet God." Then again: "is there one among you who is not stripped of envy? I say unto you that such an one is not prepared." Verse 29 adds a third case and verse 30 a fourth, about mocking a brother. The record turns the diagnostic into a checklist by supplying, in each case, what a failed answer means.

verses.label: v. 62
verses.title: Two audiences, two registers, named together
verses.text: The chapter ends by stating its own mode of address and dividing it: "I speak by way of command unto you that belong to the church; and unto those who do not belong to the church I speak by way of invitation." Membership determines whether the preceding sixty-one verses have been orders or offers. The record makes the distinction explicit only at the end, after the sermon has been delivered to both groups at once.

chapter.title: The sermon is built out of questions because statements would let the hearer agree
chapter.text: A congregation can nod at a doctrine. It cannot nod at "have you experienced this mighty change in your hearts" without answering privately first. The form is doing the work that the content could not do alone.

chapter.title: The fathers get resolved; the living are left holding it
chapter.text: Every thing asked about the previous generation is settled in the next sentence: not destroyed, loosed, saved. From verse 14 onward the grammar is identical and the resolutions stop arriving. A dozen consecutive demands are left standing open, and the chapter never returns to close them.

chapter.title: The whole argument runs on a change that already happened once
chapter.text: His father believed Abinadi and a mighty change was wrought in his heart; the fathers heard his father and the same thing happened to them. Alma is not describing something new. He is asking a congregation whether the thing that made them a congregation is still true of them.

chapter.title: "Can ye feel so now" is the hinge of the chapter
chapter.text: Verse 26 concedes the past tense in full and then moves the question to the present. Everything before it is history and everything after it is urgency, and the pivot takes four words.

chapter.title: Preparation is described as removal
chapter.text: Stripped of pride. Stripped of envy. Garments washed, cleansed, made white. The sermon never asks anyone to acquire anything; it asks them to have things taken off. Even the questions are subtractive. They remove the answer the hearer walked in with.

chapter.title: The sermon offers exactly two positions and refuses a middle
chapter.text: Verse 39 asks whose sheep you are if not the good shepherd's and answers it in the same breath. Nothing in the sermon offers a neutral position, and the wages in verse 42 are paid by whichever voice you followed.

chapter.title: He submits his own credentials to the same test
chapter.text: Having asked the congregation how it knows what it claims, he asks the question of himself in verse 45 and answers it in detail: fasting, prayer, many days, the Spirit. A man demanding private certainty from others describes how he got his own.

chapter.title: Role in the book
chapter.text: Alma 5 is the first and longest of the sermons that occupy the next twelve chapters, and it sets their method: history, then questions, then the two ways, then testimony. The last verse also sets the pattern for what follows: command inside the church, invitation outside it. Alma 6 is the administrative record of what this sermon produced.

applications.title: Start with what you already owe
applications.text: Before a single question he walks them back through their own deliverances. Memory of specific help received is a better foundation for self-examination than guilt is.

applications.title: Ask instead of tell, when the answer has to be private
applications.text: He could have described what a converted person looks like. He asked whether they were one. Some things cannot be received from outside; they can only be checked from inside.

applications.title: Put the question in the present tense
applications.text: He grants everything about their past and then asks about today. Any account of yourself that runs entirely on something that happened years ago has a tense problem.

applications.title: Measure preparation by what has come off
applications.text: Stripped of pride, stripped of envy. The test is what is no longer on you, a much harder thing to report and a much easier thing to know.

applications.title: Say how you know
applications.text: He does not simply assert; he describes the fasting, the prayer, the days, and names the source. A claim that comes with its own method attached is worth more than one delivered from authority.

applications.title: Notice which voice you actually followed
applications.text: Works are the evidence. Bringing forth good works means you hearkened to a particular voice. Look at what you produced this month and reason backwards to what you were listening to.

applications.title: Change the mode for the people who never promised
applications.text: Command to those inside, invitation to those outside. Holding people to obligations they did not take on is a category error, and the sermon corrects it in its own last sentence.

questions.text: What deliverance in my own history have I stopped sufficiently remembering?
If someone looked at my face, what would they say was engraven there?
I could once say it. Can I feel so now?
What would have to come off before I could say I was prepared?
How do I know what I say I know, and could I describe the method out loud?
Whose need have I turned my back on while my substance stayed where it was?
